Going to (7,2,2) would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going to (6,4,1) would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (4,2,1).
Going to (2,2,1) would strand number 4: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes to (4,1,2).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,1,2).
Going to (1,2,2) would leave number 5 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going to (2,2,1) would leave number 5 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (2,1,4).
The line must go to (2,1,6): to (1,2,4) is number 24, which comes later.
I can't rule out to (4,1,6), to (2,2,7) or to (1,2,6) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (4,1,6).
Going to (4,2,7), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes to (6,1,6).
I can't rule out to (6,2,7) or to (7,2,6) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (6,2,7).

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going to (7,2,6), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going to (4,2,7) would leave number 6 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going to (6,4,7), the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (7,4,6). So my guess (to (6,2,7) from cell (6,1,6)) was wrong, so the line must go to (7,2,6).
Going to (7,4,6), the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (6,4,7). So the line goes to (6,2,7).
Going to (4,2,7) would leave number 6 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (6,4,7).
Going to (6,6,7) would leave number 6 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (7,4,6).
Number 6 is next and right here, so the line takes it.

Going to (7,4,2) would strand number 7: it would be left with only one free neighbour; going to (7,6,4) would strand number 7: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes to (7,2,4).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (7,2,2).
Going to (6,4,1) would leave number 8 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (7,6,2).
Number 8 is only reachable this way.

Cell (6,4,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (4,4,1).

Number 11 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Number 12 is only reachable this way.
The line must go to (7,6,4): to (6,7,6) is number 14, which comes later.
Going to number 14, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 15. So the line goes to (6,6,7).
Number 14 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going to (2,4,7) would force the line onto number 23 before its turn. So the line goes to (2,7,6).
Number 18 is only reachable this way.
Going to (1,4,6), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes to (1,6,4).
Cell (2,7,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,7,2).
Going to number 21, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 22. So the line goes to (1,6,2).
Number 21 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Cell (2,2,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (1,2,2).
Going to (1,2,6) would wall in number 24, the last number. So the line goes to (2,4,7).
Going to (2,2,7) would leave both cell (1,2,6) and cell (4,2,7) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes to (4,4,7).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (4,2,7).
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
